audit_boundary.point_carrier: A set P of exactly n distinct point labels
audit_boundary.face_carrier: t disjoint classes of indexed face nodes, each class containing exactly N nodes
audit_boundary.certificate: Each class is ordered. Every face is a three-element subset of P. For every face after the first, a designated point lies in that face and in no earlier face of that class. The first face has three distinct points. Different face labels may have equal point sets across different classes.
audit_boundary.incidence_graph: The finite simple bipartite graph on the disjoint union of P and all tN face labels, with an edge for each point membership in its face
audit_boundary.subgraph_quantifier: Every vertex and edge subgraph Q of the incidence graph with v(Q)>=3, including non-induced subgraphs and retained isolated vertices
audit_boundary.density_convention: d2(Q)=(e(Q)-1)/(v(Q)-2) with ordinary signed integer subtraction followed by real division; the eligible denominator is positive
audit_boundary.conclusion: J is connected and remains connected after deletion of any one point or face node, hence is 2-vertex-connected. Its counts are v=(t+1)N+2, e=3tN and beta=e-v+1=(2t-1)N-1. Its 2-density is d=(3tN-1)/((t+1)N), attained only by the whole graph. Consequently J is strictly 2-balanced.
accepted_primitives: The supplied earliest-retained-face/fresh-point argument for every nonempty selected subcollection
Connectivity preserved when new vertices attach to an already connected graph
Finite induction on the exposure prefix
Elementary rational inequalities, positive-denominator cross multiplication and equality conditions
non_goals: Novelty or priority of this elementary generalized certificate theorem
Sidorenko failure of any member of the family
Existence of a simple distinct-pointset family for every pair N,t
Random Turan results or external analytic transfer

obligation_graph.rule: Combine counts, vertex-deletion connectivity and universal strict density comparison
Induct on an exposure prefix on its exposed point carrier
Partition by selected point count, then by selected face count
Take the earliest retained face and the distinct later globally fresh points

critical_findings: No demonstrated failing obligation or counterexample was found in the supplied route.

Saturation is essential: N faces on exactly N+2 ambient point labels forces each full class to cover all points and each later face to add exactly one point. Merely possessing a freshness certificate on an arbitrarily larger ambient point set would not establish the stated connectivity.

The connectivity induction must run on the exposed prefix point carrier, not on all n ambient points before they have been exposed. Future ambient point labels would otherwise be isolated vertices. This is an explicit scope clarification of the supplied route, not an additional hypothesis.

The two old points of each new face need only belong to the previous union; they need not be contained together in one earlier face. The supplied connectivity route uses only the former fact. No stronger tight-hypergraph-tree premise is required.

The face-deletion route depends on t>=2 and on disjoint indexed classes. It uses a different complete class that still spans all point labels. Repeated point sets across distinct face labels do not invalidate this step.

For t=3 and x=1, the upper rational bound is constant in b. It is still strictly below the whole-graph density when N>1. If N=1, b>=3 and b<=tN force b=3, and equality requires all nine edges. There is no exceptional proper maximizer.
The cases a=0,1,2 must be checked separately. Eligibility v>=3 supplies b>=3,2,1 respectively and makes all used denominators positive.

Equality of selected counts forces equality of the actual finite vertex and incidence carriers. This includes proper edge selections on the whole vertex carrier and is not restricted to induced subgraphs.

For distinct pointset face families, existence imposes an additional combinatorial feasibility constraint. For example N=1,t>=2 is realizable as an indexed incidence graph K_(3,t), but not as a simple triangular hypergraph with distinct face point sets. The theorem is conditional on the supplied certificate and makes no universal realization claim.
